questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to find a less stressful job
Mental health problems at work and their cost
The history of World Mental Health Day
How the royal family works with charities
questions.why: Neil says they're focusing on the topic of mental health at work.

questions.q: According to Georgina, why can mental health issues be hard to understand?
options: They are very rare
Doctors don't agree about them
There is no physical sign of them
People never talk about them
questions.why: She says unlike a broken leg, with mental health issues there's no physical sign.

questions.q: Why has mental health been getting more publicity recently?
options: Members of the British royal family have talked about it
A new law was passed to protect workers with mental illness
Businesses have started paying for therapy for their staff
A famous film about depression was released last year
questions.why: Neil says members of the British royal family have been talking about it.

questions.q: How much does Paul Farmer say poor mental health costs UK businesses each year?
options: About £3 billion
Around £300,000
More than £100 billion
Between £33 and £42 billion
questions.why: He says it costs between 33 and 42 billion pounds a year.

questions.q: How many people stop working each year because of poor mental health, according to Paul Farmer?
options: About 30,000
About 3 million
About 300,000
About 50,000
questions.why: He says 'round about 300,000 people fall out of work every year'.

questions.q: Why is losing these workers a problem for companies, according to Georgina?
options: New staff cost money to train, and experience is lost
The workers take important company secrets with them
The government fines the companies for every worker lost
Customers stop buying their products and use competitors
questions.why: She says it costs more to recruit and train new staff, and experience can't always be replaced.

questions.q: According to Geoff McDonald, what has really changed things?
options: Better medicine
More money for charities
Shorter working hours
People sharing their own stories
questions.why: He says what's really changed is people telling their stories.

questions.q: What does Geoff McDonald mean by comparing each story to a lifeboat?
options: Stories are dangerous for the people who hear them
Stories help silent sufferers see they're not alone
Sufferers should take a relaxing holiday by the sea
Only a small number of people can ever be helped
questions.why: People suffering in silence 'cling on to that lifeboat and they realise they're not alone'.
